recipes.name: Coconut Tilapia with Apricot Dipping Sauce

steps.text: Toss together the coconut, flour and Creole seasoning in a bowl. In a separate bowl, toss the tilapia with the cornstarch, and shake off the excess. Pour the egg substitute into a separate bowl, and dip the fillets in the egg. Press fillets in the coconut mixture coating all sides.

Heat canola oil in a frying pan to a temperature of about 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Fry fillets one or two at a time on both sides until golden brown. Remove to drain on a paper towel. Prepare the apricot dipping sauce by stirring together the jam, mustard, and horseradish in a small bowl. Serve the tilapia accompanied by the dipping sauce.

raw_recipe.headline: Coconut Tilapia with Apricot Dipping Sauce
raw_recipe.description: Tilapia is coated with a spicy coconut mixture and served with an apricot dipping sauce, delicious and easy! After having coconut shrimp at a famous restaurant here in Phoenix, I decided to recreate it at home using a mild white fish filet and tilapia was my first choice. Sit back and enjoy the compliments.

review.reviewBody: MMMMmm... delicious! A tip for easier coating, use tongs OR your left hand to dip in the egg, and let all the excess drip off before placing into the coconut mixture. Then use your right hand to sprinkle some of the coconut over the top and press down into it, flip and press down again. This method will help you avoid getting a battered and breaded "club hand", the term used by chefs for this problem! Line up the corn starch dip, egg dip, coconut mix and then a plate ready for the finished fillets. You can do this "assembly line" process beforehand, then refrigerate till ready to fry. This also makes the coating stick MUCH better! A little resturant tip.

This is a WONDERFUL way to cook tilapia! My family enjoyed it from the very first bite. It was very easy to make, yet elegant to eat. I made a few adjustments and it turned out perfectly. First, I cut the tilapia loin fillets in half (easier to work with) for 8 nice pieces. I used Baker's Angel Flake sweetened coconut, right out of the package (not finely chopped). It made the texture perfect and crispy (see my photo above). I used 1 whole, beaten, egg in place of the substitute and I put the cornstarch and tilapia pieces into a large ziplock bag and shook them to coat. Tongs were a great suggestion for removing the tilapia from the cornstarch baggie and dipping in the egg and coconut without a mess. To cut down on fat, I baked them in a pyrex dish sprayed with olive oil Pam (also a very light spray on top of the fish to help it crisp up!) @ about 350* for about 20-30 mins. I did not flip them or anything and they were perfectly cooked and crispy on the outside and moist on the inside without being greasy. 
The Apricot Dipping Sauce is amazing! My mom who ALWAYS and ONLY eats fish with tarter sauce said that "THIS was way better!" 
Thanks for this recipe, it is easy, elegant and super delish! A new favorite in my house!

Like other reviewers, I could only find sweetened shredded coconut at my grocery store. However, I thought the end result was delicious just the same.

I baked my tilapia for 10 minutes at 425ºF without flipping sides. Also, I used one real egg (beaten) instead of the substitute, and it turned out just fine.

This was fantastic!! My husband asked me if I made these or bought them that's how good they are! Even my son who strongly dislikes fish loved this! Few tips: I baked mine at 350 for 20 minutes and sprayed the fillets with pam to keep them from drying out; per another reviewer's suggestion. I think you could take the cornstarch down to about 1/3 cup (I hate wasting ingredients. I had leftover, after 5 fillets, that I just had to throw out.) I didn't have egg substitute so I beat 2 eggs with about 1 TBSP of water added. Also I almost had enough coconut mixture to do 5 fillets so I just eyed the ingredients and added a bit more to cover the 5th fillet. I didn't have the apricot jam or the horseradish sauce so instead I used about 1/4 cup of orange marmalade and 1/4 c of some home made jacked up peach pecan jelly and I used a packet of Arby's horsey sauce, and 1tsp sweet & Hot mustard from Trader Joes, but that made it a little too sweet so I ended up adding 2 tsp of spicy brown mustard and it was yummo!!! So I think the sauce recipe is a little forgiving if you want to use what you have on hand!

Original review 2/1/12 - I made this cutting way back on the cornstarch and oil and used one regular egg instead of the substitute. I used just about 1 T. cornstarch for the two filets I was making and cut the oil to about 2 T. I didn’t make the dipping sauce as I had another dipping sauce on hand I wanted to use. But I have made this sauce in the past for shrimp and I can say it is excellent! A word of caution – watch your heat when frying this fish as the coconut can burn very easily. UPDATE 5/8/16: I made this again baking it in a 375 degree oven. It was good, but if I decide to bake this again, I'll only coat one side of the fish with the coconut mixture, as the bottom got a little soggy. Still good though.

I have never cooked fish before in our 7 years of marriage and this was a great recipe to start with! It was delicious and my husband and I thoroughly enjoyed it. I used tips from reviews, so here's some of the things I did....I cooked two fillets and split them down the middle...it did make the fillets manageable as stated. Instead of half a cup of corn starch, I put 2 tbsp in a baggie, placed the fillets inside and shook the bag. I tried 1 tbsp, but it wasn't enough for 2 fillets. Instead of a tbsp of creole seasoning, I used a tsp and it was perfect. I cut the coconut in half, using 1/2 cup, since I only had two fillets, and chopped it in my handy chopper. I think next time I'll use a little more coconut because it was barely enough. I used one egg but want to try just egg whites next time. I pan fried it in 2 tbsp of olive oil and it fried up beautifully, making the coconut nice and crispy. I have an electric stove and put the setting on "8", one notch down from high. I ended up frying it between a 6 and a 7, as the coconut began browning a little too soon on 8. It still tasted delicious and I can't wait to make this again!

Definitely will make again. I followed reviewers suggestions ( pan fried but way less oil). Just apricot jam, Dijon mustard and 2 tsp OJ in sauce, based on what I had. I had Cajun spice on hand so put that in flour mixture. I had cod on hand, not tilapia. Just love having another way to make fish!

This was pretty amazing. I put the crust mixture the food processor to get it fine. And it stuck nicely to the fish for a crispy finish! I also used coconut oil for frying. It turned out nicely! I will probably add cayenne pepper to it nice time as I enjoy a little heat!

This was awesome! I was looking for something different to do with my fish & luckily I found this recipe. I pulsed the coconut mixture in my food processor & that gave it the perfect consistency. I baked the fish at 350 for about 15-20min & it was crispy perfect. I also used the coconut to coat some zucchini, the fried it in olive oil. Yummy! I'll definitely use this recipe again.
Cooked in oven for 20 min. Turned halfway through. Dip didn't have horseradish and it was peach jelly. Very good

Yummy! Wow, this recipe exceeded my expectations! The only change in the recipe was with the sauce I heated up the ingredients on the stove and added 2 TBL of Orange juice to it. It made the sauce a little sweeter and really brought out the spice in the mustard & horseradish.

Followed commenter AJ West's tips for breading, which were really helpful! Cooked the tilapia in coconut oil, since I had it, which really enhanced the coconut flavor, and since the recipe didn't specify unsweetened or sweetened coconut, I went with sweetened. Absolutely delicious! This is going into our regular meal rotation.
Tasty and easy! I used the "bake in oven" at 350 for 25min. Worked very well.

I used corn starch in place of the flour to keep it gluten free, real egg, and fried in avocado oil instead of canola. We’re landlocked so not really a fish-loving family unless we’re visiting the coast, but this will be a repeat recipe with cod, shrimp, and cat fish as well as talapia here!
Best fish dish ever. Used a fig jam and Kozlik's horseradish mustard the first time I made this. Could not find a creole seasoning but found a recipe for it, easy enough. Delish!!!
scrumptious!! I didn't have apricot jam, so I used peach and orange...worked great! Do let it brown on each side....so crispy!!
I used white rice flour, recklessly mixed the ingredients in a hurry, and coated white bass. The apricot sauce was icing on the coconut cake.

This is so tasty. Most of my my family is not fans of fish but they loved this. I used 2 real eggs and added Creole powder and chili flakes. I also used a bit more horseradish and Dijon to the apricot jam to make it less sweet. Excellent recipe!
My picky son didn’t like the apricot sauce but he rated the fish 1000. I made it as described except I used vegetable oil as I do not buy canola oil. It turned out great.

WOW! Great tasting and so easy to make. Only diverted slightly from original recipe by spraying with oil after coating in coconut mixture , placed on a lightly greased cookie sheet, and baked it.
Thanks for sharing!!
